title: Antioxidants and Exercise Performance: With a Focus on Vitamin E and C Supplementation
authors: Madalyn Riley Higgins, Azimeh Izadi, Mojtaba Kaviani
source: International Journal of Environmental Research and Public Health
abstract: This paper reviews antioxidant supplementation, specifically vitamins E and C, for exercise performance. Evidence suggests supplementation may hinder exercise adaptations and is generally not beneficial, except in specific circumstances.

title: Vitamin C and E supplementation does not affect heat shock proteins or endogenous antioxidants in trained skeletal muscles during 12 weeks of strength training
authors: K. T. Cumming, T. Raastad, A. Sørstrøm, M. P. Paronetto, N. Mercatelli, I. Ugelstad, D. Caporossi, G...
abstract: This study examined the impact of vitamin C and E supplementation on trained individuals undergoing strength training. The supplementation did not alter acute exercise stress responses or long-term adaptations in heat shock proteins or endogenous antioxidants.

title: Antioxidant supplements and endurance exercise: Current evidence and mechanistic insights
authors: Shaun A. Mason, Adam J. Trewin, Lewan Parker, Glenn D. Wadley
abstract: This review examines antioxidant supplements for endurance athletes. Most supplements lack evidence for performance enhancement, with some potentially hindering training adaptations.

title: The Effects of Strength Training Combined with Vitamin C and E Supplementation on Skeletal Muscle Mass and Strength: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
authors: Maurilio T. Dutra, Wagner Rodrigues Martins, Alexandre L. A. Ribeiro, Martim Bottaro
abstract: This systematic review and meta-analysis examined studies on vitamin C and E supplementation combined with strength training. The findings suggest these supplements do not enhance muscle strength or mass and may even attenuate hypertrophy.

title: Effects of Acute Vitamin C plus Vitamin E Supplementation on Exercise-Induced Muscle Damage in Runners: A Double-Blind Randomized Controlled Trial
authors: María Martínez-Ferrán, Víctor Cuadrado-Peñafiel, Juan Manuel Sánchez-Andreo, Marta Villar-Lucas, Món...
abstract: This study investigated if vitamin C and E supplementation reduces exercise-induced muscle damage in runners. The supplementation did not significantly improve muscle damage markers or performance compared to a placebo.

title: Vitamin C and E Treatment Blunts Sprint Interval Training–Induced Changes in Inflammatory Mediator-, Calcium-, and Mitochondria-Related Signaling in Recreationally Active Elderly Humans
authors: Victoria L. Wyckelsma, Tomas Venckunas, Marius Brazaitis, Stefano Gastaldello, Audrius Snieckus, Ner...
abstract: Sprint interval training in elderly individuals was studied with and without antioxidant treatment. Antioxidants blunted training-induced cellular signaling changes in muscle, but did not affect performance outcomes.

title: Do Antioxidant Vitamins Prevent Exercise-Induced Muscle Damage? A Systematic Review
authors: María Martinez-Ferran, Fabian Sanchis-Gomar, Carl J. Lavie, Giuseppe Lippi, Helios Pareja-Galeano
abstract: This systematic review examined vitamin C and E supplementation's effects on exercise-induced muscle damage. The available data are not conclusive regarding whether these vitamins prevent muscle damage.

title: Supplementation with Vitamins C and E and Exercise-Induced Delayed-Onset Muscle Soreness: A Systematic Review
authors: María F. Torre, María Martinez-Ferran, Néstor Vallecillo, Sergio L. Jiménez, Carlos Romero-Morales, ...
abstract: This systematic review examined vitamin C and E supplementation's effect on exercise-induced muscle soreness. The evidence is insufficient to confirm these vitamins minimize delayed-onset muscle soreness.

title: Differences in the Pro/Antioxidative Status and Cellular Stress Response in Elderly Women after 6 Weeks of Exercise Training Supported by 1000 mg of Vitamin C Supplementation
authors: Małgorzata Żychowska, Ewa Sadowska-Krępa, Elisabetta Damiani, Luca Tiano, Ewa Ziemann, Alicja Nowak-...
abstract: This study examined the effects of exercise training with vitamin C supplementation on antioxidant status and cellular stress response in elderly women. Vitamin C supplementation increased oxidative stress markers and influenced minor changes in gene expression related to training adaptation.

title: Antioxidant Supplementation Hinders the Role of Exercise Training as a Natural Activator of SIRT1
authors: Carmine Sellitto, Graziamaria Corbi, Berenice Stefanelli, Valentina Manzo, Marta Trucillo, Bruno Cha...
abstract: Exercise training increases SIRT1 levels, which boosts the body's antioxidant system. However, antioxidant supplements appear to interfere with this exercise-induced activation of SIRT1.

title: Vitamin C and E Treatment Blocks Changes in Kynurenine Metabolism Triggered by Three Weeks of Sprint Interval Training in Recreationally Active Elderly Humans
authors: Victoria L. Wyckelsma, Ada Trepci, Lilly Schwieler, Tomas Venckunas, Marius Brazaitis, Sigitas Kaman...
abstract: Sprint interval training in elderly men altered kynurenine pathway metabolism towards neuroprotection. This beneficial shift was prevented by concurrent vitamin C and E supplementation.

title: Exercise Training and Vitamin C Supplementation Affects Ferritin mRNA in Leukocytes without Affecting Prooxidative/Antioxidative Balance in Elderly Women
authors: Małgorzata Żychowska, Agata Grzybkowska, Monika Wiech, Robert Urbański, Wanda Pilch, Anna Piotrowska...
abstract: Exercise training with vitamin C supplementation decreased ferritin mRNA in elderly women's leukocytes. This intervention did not alter the prooxidative/antioxidative balance.

title: Potential harms of supplementation with high doses of antioxidants in athletes
authors: Shunchang Li, Babatunde Fasipe, Ismail Laher
abstract: This paper reviews the use of high-dose antioxidant supplements by athletes. It concludes that these supplements may hinder beneficial training adaptations and potentially cause harm.

title: Can Low-Dose of Dietary Vitamin E Supplementation Reduce Exercise-Induced Muscle Damage and Oxidative Stress? A Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials
authors: Myunghee Kim, Hyeyoon Eo, Josephine Gahyun Lim, Hyunjung Lim, Yunsook Lim
abstract: This meta-analysis examined the effects of vitamin E supplementation on exercise-induced muscle damage. Low-dose vitamin E, especially under 500 IU, was found to reduce muscle damage, particularly in athletes.

title: A Comparison of the Antioxidant Effects Between Hydrogen Gas Inhalation and Vitamin C Supplementation in Response to a 60-Min Treadmill Exercise in Rat Gastrocnemius Muscle
authors: Li Chaoqun, Zhao Yuqi, Zhou Shi, Yu Zhenghui, Wen Li
abstract: Hydrogen gas inhalation and vitamin C were compared for their antioxidant effects on rat gastrocnemius muscle after treadmill exercise. Hydrogen gas reduced oxidative stress without blunting mitochondrial biogenesis signals, unlike vitamin C.

title: Enhanced Antioxidative Defense by Vitamins C and E Consumption Prevents 7-Day High-Salt Diet-Induced Microvascular Endothelial Function Impairment in Young Healthy Individuals
authors: Lidija Barić, Ines Drenjančević, Martina Mihalj, Anita Matić, Marko Stupin, Luka Kolar, Zrinka Mihal...
abstract: This study investigated if vitamins C and E prevent high-salt diet-induced microvascular dysfunction in healthy individuals. The findings show these vitamins prevented the diet's negative effects on endothelial function by mitigating oxidative stress.

title: Elastic resistance training is more effective than vitamin D3 supplementation in reducing oxidative stress and strengthen antioxidant enzymes in healthy men
authors: Fardin Kalvandi, Mohammad Ali Azarbayjani, Ronak Azizbeigi, Kamal Azizbeigi
abstract: Elastic resistance training was studied with and without vitamin D3 supplementation in healthy men. Elastic resistance training alone was more effective than with vitamin D3 supplementation for reducing oxidative stress and strengthening antioxidant enzymes.

title: Vitamin D 3  supplementation does not enhance the effects of resistance training in older adults
authors: Knut Sindre Mølmen, Daniel Hammarström, Karianne Pedersen, Anne Cecilie Lian Lie, Ragnvald B. Steile...
source: Journal of Cachexia, Sarcopenia and Muscle
abstract: This study investigated the effects of vitamin D3 supplementation on resistance training outcomes in older adults. Vitamin D3 supplementation did not enhance improvements in muscle strength, mass, or endurance compared to placebo.

title: Exercise Training and Skeletal Muscle Antioxidant Enzymes: An Update
authors: Scott K. Powers, Erica Goldstein, Matthew Schrager, Li Li Ji
abstract: This review summarizes how endurance, interval, and resistance exercise training increase skeletal muscle antioxidant enzymes. This upregulation protects against exercise-induced oxidative damage, potentially delaying fatigue and improving performance.

title: An Overview of Physical Exercise and Antioxidant Supplementation Influences on Skeletal Muscle Oxidative Stress
authors: Shima Taherkhani, Kosar Valaei, Hamid Arazi, Katsuhiko Suzuki
abstract: This paper reviews how exercise and antioxidant supplements affect skeletal muscle oxidative stress. Findings are paradoxical due to varied study designs, necessitating further research.

title: Antioxidant Supplementation Modulates Neutrophil Inflammatory Response to Exercise-Induced Stress
authors: Lucrecia Carrera-Quintanar, Lorena Funes, María Herranz-López, Pascual Martínez-Peinado, Sandra Pasc...
abstract: This study investigated the inflammatory response to exercise and the effect of antioxidant supplements. Antioxidant supplementation appeared to alter neutrophil inflammatory marker release, potentially influencing post-exercise recovery.

title: Can vitamin C supplementation reverse the effects of exercise training in polluted air on oxidative stress markers? A randomized controlled trial
authors: Amin Eatemadyboroujeni, Mehdi Kargarfard, Hojatollah Alaei
abstract: This study investigated the effects of exercise, polluted air, and vitamin C on oxidative stress markers in rats. Vitamin C supplementation did not significantly reverse the increased oxidative stress caused by exercise in polluted air.

title: Effect of Vitamins C and E Co-Supplementation on Serum C-Reactive Protein Level: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials
authors: Faezeh Fouladvand, Ebrahim Falahi, Omid Asbaghi, Amir Abbasnezhad
abstract: This systematic review and meta-analysis examined vitamin C and E co-supplementation's effect on C-reactive protein. Co-supplementation did not significantly impact CRP overall, but reduced it in those aged 30 and over.

title: Synergistic Effects of Exercise Training and Vitamin D Supplementation on Mitochondrial Function of Cardiac Tissue, Antioxidant Capacity, and Tumor Growth in Breast Cancer in Bearing-4T1 Mice
authors: Ali Jafari, Dariush Sheikholeslami-Vatani, Farnoosh Khosrobakhsh, Neda Khaledi
abstract: This study examined the effects of exercise and vitamin D on breast cancer mice. Combining exercise and vitamin D inhibited tumor growth, improved antioxidant capacity, and positively modulated cardiac gene expression.

title: Astaxanthin supplementation enhances metabolic adaptation with aerobic training in the elderly
authors: Sophia Z. Liu, Ana P. Valencia, Matt P. VanDoren, Eric G. Shankland, Baback Roshanravan, Kevin E. Co...
abstract: Astaxanthin supplementation was studied alongside aerobic training in elderly adults to assess its impact on metabolic adaptation. The study found astaxanthin enhanced specific muscle endurance and fat oxidation, particularly in males.

title: Polyphenol Supplementation and Antioxidant Status in Athletes: A Narrative Review
authors: Aleksandra Bojarczuk, Magdalena Dzitkowska-Zabielska
abstract: This review examined polyphenol supplementation's effects on athletes' antioxidant status and exercise performance. The available evidence does not conclusively support widespread polyphenol supplementation for athletes, indicating a need for further research.

title: Oxidative Stress, Mitochondrial Function and Adaptation to Exercise: New Perspectives in Nutrition
authors: Nancy Vargas-Mendoza, Marcelo Angeles-Valencia, Ángel Morales-González, Eduardo Osiris Madrigal-Sant...
abstract: This paper reviews how mitochondria adapt to exercise-induced energy demands and oxidative stress. It explores whether nutrients, particularly antioxidants, might interfere with this adaptation or exercise performance.

title: Effect of Antioxidant Supplementation on Markers of Oxidative Stress and Muscle Damage after Strength Exercise: A Systematic Review
authors: Cristina Canals-Garzón, Rafael Guisado-Barrilao, Darío Martínez-García, Ignacio Jesús Chirosa-Ríos, ...
abstract: This systematic review examined antioxidant supplementation's effects on oxidative stress and muscle damage after strength exercise. Antioxidants like pomegranate juice and taurine showed beneficial effects, potentially reducing fatigue and speeding recovery.

title: Effects of Vitamin E and Coenzyme Q 10  Supplementation on Oxidative Stress Parameters in Untrained Leisure Horses Subjected to Acute Moderate Exercise
authors: Alenka Nemec Svete, Tomaž Vovk, Mojca Bohar Topolovec, Peter Kruljc
abstract: This study investigated vitamin E and CoQ10 supplementation in untrained horses undergoing exercise. Vitamin E, alone or combined with CoQ10, prevented exercise-induced lipid peroxidation.

title: Effect of exercise and antioxidant supplementation on cellular lipid peroxidation in elderly individuals: Systematic review and network meta-analysis
authors: Chunxia Ni, Yiyi Ji, Keke Hu, Kai Xing, Yining Xu, Yanan Gao
abstract: This systematic review and network meta-analysis examined exercise and antioxidant supplementation's effects on cellular lipid peroxidation in the elderly. A combination of aerobic and resistance exercise with placebo intake most effectively reduced lipid peroxidation.

title: Reactive oxygen species in exercise and insulin resistance: Working towards personalized antioxidant treatment
authors: Kathryn McKeegan, Shaun A. Mason, Adam J. Trewin, Michelle A. Keske, Glenn D. Wadley, Paul A. Della ...
abstract: This review examines human research on antioxidant treatment for insulin resistance and glycemic control. Personalized antioxidant strategies are needed, considering context, individual deficiencies, and antioxidant properties, to improve effectiveness.

title: Effect of six weeks 1000 mg/day vitamin C supplementation and healthy training in elderly women on genes expression associated with the immune response - a randomized controlled trial
authors: Małgorzata Żychowska, Agata Grzybkowska, Mariusz Zasada, Anna Piotrowska, Danuta Dworakowska, Olga C...
source: Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition
abstract: This study examined the effect of vitamin C supplementation and exercise on immune gene expression in elderly women. While most genes showed no significant change, vitamin C supplementation showed a tendency to alter IL-6 and IL-10 expression.

title: Vitamin E Supplementation and Mitochondria in Experimental and Functional Hyperthyroidism: A Mini-Review
authors: Gaetana Napolitano, Gianluca Fasciolo, Sergio Di Meo, Paola Venditti
abstract: This mini-review examines vitamin E's role in protecting mitochondria from oxidative damage in hyperthyroidism. Vitamin E supplementation limits hyperthyroidism-induced mitochondrial ROS and oxidative damage, preserving cell function.

title: Well-Trained Elders Have Antioxidant Responses and an Equal Magnitude of EIMD as Young Adults
authors: Eva Tékus, Nikolett Lilla Szénási, Edina Szabó, Zoltan Heckel, Tibor Mintál, Tamas Kőszegi, Tamas At...
abstract: This study examined antioxidant responses and muscle damage markers in young and older men after eccentric training. No significant differences in antioxidant capacity or muscle damage were found between the groups, suggesting similar adaptability.

title: Endogenous and Exogenous Antioxidants in Skeletal Muscle Fatigue Development during Exercise
authors: Elżbieta Supruniuk, Jan Górski, Adrian Chabowski
abstract: This paper reviews the dual role of reactive oxygen and nitrogen species in skeletal muscle fatigue during exercise. It concludes that both exercise-induced and antioxidant-supplemented ROS/RNS levels can impact muscle function by influencing signaling pathways and redox balance.

title: The Effect of Combined Vitamin C and Vitamin E Supplementation on Oxidative Stress Markers in Women with Endometriosis: A Randomized, Triple-Blind Placebo-Controlled Clinical Trial
authors: Leila Amini, Razieh Chekini, Mohammad Reza Nateghi, Hamid Haghani, Tannaz Jamialahmadi, Thozhukat Sa...
abstract: This study investigated the effects of combined vitamin C and E supplementation on oxidative stress and pain in women with endometriosis. The supplementation significantly reduced oxidative stress markers and pelvic pain symptoms.

title: Effect of carbohydrate–protein supplementation on endurance training adaptations
authors: Abdullah F. Alghannam, Iain Templeman, Joel E. Thomas, Dawid Jedrzejewski, Samuel Griffiths, Joseph ...
abstract: This study investigated the effect of post-exercise carbohydrate-protein supplementation on endurance training adaptations in men and women. Post-exercise protein supplementation increased mTOR gene expression, but did not enhance improvements in maximal oxygen uptake compared to carbohydrate-only supplementation.

title: Targeted Antioxidants in Exercise-Induced Mitochondrial Oxidative Stress: Emphasis on DNA Damage
authors: Josh Williamson, Gareth Davison
abstract: This review examines mitochondria-targeted antioxidants and their potential to mitigate exercise-induced mitochondrial oxidative stress, particularly DNA damage. Targeted antioxidants offer a promising approach to address this damage, unlike non-selective antioxidants.

title: Pterostilbene Enhances Endurance Capacity via Promoting Skeletal Muscle Adaptations to Exercise Training in Rats
authors: Jiawei Zheng, Wujian Liu, Xiaohui Zhu, Li Ran, Hedong Lang, Long Yi, Mantian Mi, Jundong Zhu
abstract: Pterostilbene (PST) was studied for its effects on skeletal muscle adaptations to exercise training in rats. PST supplementation enhanced exercise-induced improvements in endurance capacity by promoting slow-twitch fiber formation, angiogenesis, and mitochondrial biogenesis.

title: Nutritional Supplements to Support Resistance Exercise in Countering the Sarcopenia of Aging
authors: James McKendry, Brad S. Currier, Changhyun Lim, Jonathan C. Mcleod, Aaron C.Q. Thomas, Stuart M. Phi...
abstract: This review examines nutritional strategies to enhance resistance training for combating age-related muscle loss. Combining resistance exercise with specific nutrients and supplements can optimize muscle growth and maintenance, supporting healthspan in older adults.

title: Supplementation of Underfed Twin-Bearing Ewes with Herbal Vitamins C and E: Impacts on Birth Weight, Postnatal Growth, and Pre-Weaning Survival of the Lambs
authors: Víctor H. Parraguez, Francisco Sales, Oscar A. Peralta, Eileen Narbona, Raúl Lira, Mónica De los Rey...
source: Animals : an Open Access Journal from MDPI
abstract: Herbal vitamins C and E, alone or with concentrate, were supplemented to underfed twin-bearing ewes. Supplementation improved lamb birth weight and antioxidant capacity, with combined treatment showing the best results.

title: How N-Acetylcysteine Supplementation Affects Redox Regulation, Especially at Mitohormesis and Sarcohormesis Level: Current Perspective
authors: Aslı Devrim-Lanpir, Lee Hill, Beat Knechtle
abstract: This review examines N-acetylcysteine's effects on exercise-induced oxidative stress and athletic adaptation. It specifically focuses on how NAC influences mitohormesis and sarcohormesis.

title: Vitamin E and Metabolic Health: Relevance of Interactions with Other Micronutrients
authors: Sijia Liao, Sylvia Oghogho Omage, Lisa Börmel, Stefan Kluge, Martin Schubert, Maria Wallert, Stefan ...
abstract: This review examines vitamin E's interactions with other micronutrients and their impact on metabolic health. These interactions may explain discrepancies in clinical trials and influence vitamin E's physiological functions.

title: Vitamin D Supplementation Has No Impact on Cardiorespiratory Fitness, but Improves Inflammatory Status in Vitamin D Deficient Young Men Engaged in Resistance Training
authors: Lauri Savolainen, Saima Timpmann, Martin Mooses, Luule Medijainen, Lisette Tõnutare, Frederik Ross, ...
abstract: Vitamin D supplementation was studied in deficient young men undergoing resistance training. It improved inflammatory status but did not affect cardiorespiratory fitness.

title: Mitochondria-targeted antioxidant supplementation improves 8 km time trial performance in middle-aged trained male cyclists
authors: S. C. Broome, A. J. Braakhuis, C. J. Mitchell, T. L. Merry
source: Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition
abstract: This study investigated the effect of MitoQ supplementation on cycling performance in trained male cyclists. MitoQ supplementation improved 8km time trial performance and increased average power output.

title: Diclofenac Administration after Physical Training Blunts Adaptations of Peripheral Systems and Leads to Losses in Exercise Performance: In Vivo and In Silico Analyses
authors: Rômulo Pillon Barcelos, Frederico Diniz Lima, Aline Alves Courtes, Ingrid Kich da Silva, Jose Eduard...
abstract: This study investigated diclofenac's impact on exercise adaptations in rats. Diclofenac blunted exercise-induced performance gains and tissue adaptations, despite reducing inflammation.

title: Housing temperature influences exercise training adaptations in mice
authors: Steffen H. Raun, Carlos Henriquez-Olguín, Iuliia Karavaeva, Mona Ali, Lisbeth L. V. Møller, Witold K...
abstract: This study investigated how housing temperature affects exercise training adaptations in mice. Thermoneutral housing reduced exercise-induced improvements in insulin action, energy expenditure, and body composition, indicating training adaptations are temperature-dependent.

title: Combined Effects of Exercise Training and Nutritional Supplementation in Cancer Patients in the Context of the COVID-19: A Perspective Study
authors: Mahdieh Molanouri Shamsi, Alieh Vahed, AmirHossin Ahmadi Hekmatikar, Katsuhiko Suzuki
abstract: This perspective study examines how exercise and nutritional supplements might affect cancer patients' COVID-19 risk. Combining these interventions could boost immune responses against COVID-19 and potentially improve vaccine efficacy.

title: Cross-Sectional Associations Between Dietary Antioxidant Vitamins C, E and Carotenoid Intakes and Sarcopenic Indices in Women Aged 18–79 Years
authors: A. A. Welch, A. Jennings, E. Kelaiditi, J. Skinner, C. J. Steves
abstract: This study examined the relationship between dietary antioxidant vitamin intake and sarcopenic indices in women. Higher vitamin C and carotenoid intake was associated with greater skeletal muscle mass and power, especially in younger women.

title: Supplementation of L-Arginine, L-Glutamine, Vitamin C, Vitamin E, Folic Acid, and Green Tea Extract Enhances Serum Nitric Oxide Content and Antifatigue Activity in Mice
authors: Yi-Ming Chen, Huashuai Li, Yen-Shuo Chiu, Chi-Chang Huang, Wen-Chyuan Chen
source: Evidence-based Complementary and Alternative Medicine : eCAM
abstract: A combined extract of L-arginine, L-glutamine, vitamins C and E, folic acid, and green tea extract was administered to mice. This supplementation increased nitric oxide content and improved exercise performance, suggesting an antifatigue effect.

title: Exercise Training Combined with  Bifidobacterium Longum  OLP-01 Supplementation Improves Exercise Physiological Adaption and Performance
authors: Wen-Ching Huang, Yi-Ju Hsu, Chi-Chang Huang, Hsuan-Chen Liu, Mon-Chien Lee
abstract: This study investigated the effects of exercise training combined with *Bifidobacterium longum* OLP-01 supplementation in mice. The combination significantly improved exercise performance, reduced fatigue markers, and ameliorated exercise-induced inflammation and injury.

title: Endurance Training Depletes Antioxidant System but Does Not Affect Endothelial Functions in Women with Abdominal Obesity: A Randomized Trial with a Comparison to Endurance-Strength Training
authors: Małgorzata Jamka, Paweł Bogdański, Patrycja Krzyżanowska-Jankowska, Anna Miśkiewicz-Chotnicka, Joann...
abstract: Endurance and endurance-strength training were compared in abdominally obese women. Endurance training depleted antioxidant systems but did not affect endothelial function, unlike endurance-strength training.

title: Vitamin C and Cardiovascular Disease: An Update
authors: Marco B. Morelli, Jessica Gambardella, Vanessa Castellanos, Valentina Trimarco, Gaetano Santulli
abstract: This review assesses studies on vitamin C's role in cardiovascular and cerebrovascular diseases. It discusses potential benefits, pitfalls, and controversies in this research area.

title: Impact of exercise training and supplemental oxygen on submaximal exercise performance in patients with COPD
authors: Daniel Neunhäuserer, Bernhard Reich, Barbara Mayr, Bernhard Kaiser, Bernd Lamprecht, David Niedersee...
source: Scandinavian Journal of Medicine & Science in Sports
abstract: This study examined the effects of exercise training with and without supplemental oxygen on COPD patients' submaximal exercise performance. Exercise training improved exercise tolerance and capacity, with supplemental oxygen having minimal additional benefits.

title: Astaxanthin-, β-Carotene-, and Resveratrol-Rich Foods Support Resistance Training-Induced Adaptation
authors: Aki Kawamura, Wataru Aoi, Ryo Abe, Yukiko Kobayashi, Masashi Kuwahata, Akane Higashi
abstract: This study investigated the effects of resistance training with nutrient-rich foods on muscle adaptation in men. Consuming foods rich in astaxanthin, β-carotene, and resveratrol enhanced strength and metabolic improvements from training.

title: Effects of Rhodiola Rosea Supplementation on Exercise and Sport: A Systematic Review
authors: Yao Lu, Bin Deng, Luhua Xu, Hanjiao Liu, Yinzhi Song, Fengxia Lin
abstract: This systematic review evaluated Rhodiola rosea supplementation for exercise and sport. Most studies found it positively impacts athletic ability and performance with no significant adverse effects.

title: The effects of endogenously‐ and exogenously‐induced hyperketonemia on exercise performance and adaptation
authors: David J. Dearlove, Adrian Soto Mota, David Hauton, Katherine Pinnick, Rhys Evans, Jack Miller, Roman...
abstract: This study compared exercise capacity and adaptation with carbohydrate-rich, ketone-supplemented, and ketogenic diets. Ketone supplementation improved exercise capacity, while a ketogenic diet impaired it and reduced insulin sensitivity.

title: Prevention of Teratogenesis in Pregnancies of Obese Rats by Vitamin E Supplementation
authors: Martin Alcala, Victoria E. Bolado, Isabel Sánchez-Vera, Sonia Clapés, Francisco Dasí, Guillermo Sáez...
abstract: Obese rats were supplemented with vitamin E to investigate its effect on teratogenesis. Vitamin E prevented malformations by maintaining maternal glutathione levels, which protected embryos from oxidative stress.

title: Mitigating the Growth, Biochemical Changes, Genotoxic and Pathological Effects of Copper Toxicity in Broiler Chickens by Supplementing Vitamins C and E
authors: Mohamed A. Hashem, Sahar S. Abd El Hamied, Eman M. A. Ahmed, Shimaa A. Amer, Mohamed E. El-Sharnouby
source: Animals : an Open Access Journal from MDPI
abstract: This study investigated the effects of copper sulfate toxicity and vitamin C/E supplementation on broiler chickens. Vitamins C and E, especially when combined, helped mitigate the negative impacts of copper toxicity on growth and liver health.

title: Randomised Controlled Trial of Fish Oil Supplementation on Responsiveness to Resistance Exercise Training in Sarcopenic Older Women
authors: Natália Maira da Cruz Alves, Karina Pfrimer, Priscila Carvalho Santos, Ellen Cristini de Freitas, Th...
abstract: This randomized controlled trial examined fish oil's effect on resistance training in sarcopenic older women. Fish oil supplementation significantly enhanced muscle strength gains compared to placebo.

title: Effects of Resistance Training on the Redox Status of Skeletal Muscle in Older Adults
authors: Paulo H. C. Mesquita, Donald A. Lamb, Joshua S. Godwin, Shelby C. Osburn, Bradley A. Ruple, Johnatho...
abstract: Resistance training in older adults increased antioxidant enzyme activity and decreased oxidative damage in skeletal muscle. This suggests multi-level regulation of muscle redox status in response to training.

title: White tea modulates antioxidant defense of endurance-trained rats
authors: Patrícia Berilli, Gustavo Bernardes Fanaro, Jéssica Piva Santos, Felix Guillermo Reyes Reyes, Amadeu...
abstract: White tea was given to endurance-trained rats to assess its impact on antioxidant defenses after exhaustive exercise. Long-term white tea consumption improved antioxidant capacity and reduced oxidative damage, suggesting a role in managing exercise-induced stress.

title: Impact of Vitamin D on Physical Efficiency and Exercise Performance—A Review
authors: Michał Wiciński, Dawid Adamkiewicz, Monika Adamkiewicz, Maciej Śniegocki, Marta Podhorecka, Paweł Sz...
abstract: This review examines vitamin D's impact on physical efficiency and exercise performance. Vitamin D influences muscle function, bone health, and immune response, potentially enhancing athletic capabilities.

title: Anti-Inflammatory Effects of a Period of Aerobic Training and Vitamin D Supplementation in Postmenopausal Women with Metabolic Syndrome
authors: Parivash Najafi Nazarabadi, Zaher Etemad, Rastegar Hoseini, Fatah Moradi
abstract: This study examined the anti-inflammatory effects of aerobic training and vitamin D supplementation in postmenopausal women with metabolic syndrome. The combination of exercise and vitamin D significantly reduced inflammatory markers and improved metabolic syndrome indices more than either intervention alone.

title: Effects of antioxidant supplementation on oxidative stress balance in young footballers- a randomized double-blind trial
authors: Błażej Stankiewicz, Mirosława Cieślicka, Sławomir Kujawski, Elżbieta Piskorska, Tomasz Kowalik, Just...
source: Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition
abstract: Young footballers were given chokeberry juice for 7 weeks to study its effect on oxidative stress. The supplementation did not significantly alter oxidative stress markers, biochemical parameters, or performance.

title: Vitamin E: Where Are We Now in Vascular Diseases?
authors: Anahita Garg, Jetty Chung-Yung Lee
abstract: This review examines vitamin E's role in vascular health, focusing on its antioxidant and regulatory effects. While its antioxidant benefits are known, its potential as a vascular regulatory molecule requires further study.

title: The Role of Vitamin C in Two Distinct Physiological States: Physical Activity and Sleep
authors: Aneta Otocka-Kmiecik, Aleksandra Król
abstract: This paper reviews the relationship between vitamin C, physical activity, and sleep. Vitamin C supplementation may benefit sleep health and aspects of physical activity, potentially by influencing oxidative stress.

title: 6-Week Supplementation with  Tribulus terrestris  L. to Trained Male CrossFit ®  Athletes on Muscle, Inflammation, and Antioxidant Biomarkers: A Randomized, Single-Blind, Placebo-Controlled Trial
authors: Diego Fernández-Lázaro, Jesús Seco-Calvo, Jorge Pascual-Fernández, Carlos Domínguez-Ortega, Miguel D...
source: International Journal of Environmental Research and Public Health
abstract: This study investigated the effects of 6-week *Tribulus terrestris* supplementation on trained male CrossFit athletes. Supplementation attenuated oxidative stress, muscle damage, and inflammation compared to placebo.

title: Effect of vitamin E supplementation on chicken sperm quality: A meta-analysis
authors: Sari Yanti Hayanti, Cecep Hidayat, Anuraga Jayanegara, Mohammad Miftakhus Sholikin, Supardi Rusdiana...
abstract: This meta-analysis examined the effect of dietary vitamin E on rooster sperm quality. Vitamin E supplementation significantly improved sperm concentration, motility, viability, and fertility, while reducing sperm death.

title: Exercise May Ameliorate the Detrimental Side Effects of High Vitamin D Supplementation on Muscle Function in Mice
authors: Danielle A Debruin, Cara A Timpani, Hannah Lalunio, Emma Rybalka, Craig A Goodman, Alan Hayes
abstract: High vitamin D supplementation reduced muscle force in sedentary mice. Exercise normalized this effect and improved fatigue resistance.

title: Rhodiola/Cordyceps -Based Herbal Supplement Promotes Endurance Training-Improved Body Composition But Not Oxidative Stress and Metabolic Biomarkers: A Preliminary Randomized Controlled Study
authors: Yi-Hung Liao, Yi-Chen Chao, Brenton Yim-Quan Sim, Hui-Mei Lin, Mu-Tsung Chen, Chung-Yu Chen
abstract: This study examined the effects of an 8-week endurance training program combined with a Rhodiola/Cordyceps supplement. The supplement enhanced improvements in body composition but did not affect oxidative stress or metabolic biomarkers compared to placebo.

title: Cardiovascular and Metabolic Protection by Vitamin E: A Matter of Treatment Strategy?
authors: Melanie Ziegler, Maria Wallert, Stefan Lorkowski, Karlheinz Peter
abstract: This paper reviews vitamin E's role in cardiovascular health, highlighting conflicting trial results. It concludes that acute vitamin E treatment, not chronic supplementation, may offer clinical benefits, particularly in acute conditions like myocardial infarction.

title: The effect of fish oil supplementation on resistance training-induced adaptations
authors: Jeffery L. Heileson, Steven B. Machek, Dillon R. Harris, Sara Tomek, Leticia C. de Souza, Adam J. Ki...
source: Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition
abstract: This study investigated the effects of fish oil supplementation on resistance training adaptations in young adults. Fish oil supplementation, compared to placebo, significantly increased bench press strength but did not significantly alter body composition or squat strength.

title: Vitamin C and Neutrophil Function: Findings from Randomized Controlled Trials
authors: Mikee Liugan, Anitra C. Carr
abstract: This review systematically analyzed randomized controlled trials on vitamin C's effects on neutrophil function. Vitamin C supplementation showed positive effects on neutrophil migration, phagocytosis, oxidative burst, and apoptosis in various patient groups and healthy individuals.

title: Ketone ester supplementation blunts overreaching symptoms during endurance training overload
authors: Chiel Poffé, Monique Ramaekers, Ruud Van Thienen, Peter Hespel
abstract: Ketone ester supplementation was studied in endurance athletes undergoing training overload. This supplementation blunted overreaching symptoms and enhanced performance.

title: Combined effects of vitamin D supplementation and endurance exercise training on insulin resistance in newly diagnosed type 2 diabetes mellitus patients with vitamin D deficiency: study protocol for a randomized controlled trial
authors: Mi Xiang, Xiaomin Sun, Junxiang Wei, Zhen-Bo Cao
abstract: This study protocol outlines a randomized controlled trial investigating the combined effects of vitamin D and endurance exercise on insulin resistance in newly diagnosed type 2 diabetes patients. The research aims to determine if this combination offers synergistic benefits beyond individual interventions.

title: Temperate performance and metabolic adaptations following endurance training performed under environmental heat stress
authors: Ed Maunder, Daniel J. Plews, Gareth A. Wallis, Matthew J. Brick, Warren B. Leigh, Wee‐Leong Chang, C...
abstract: Endurance training in 33°C versus 18°C was studied in trained males. Training in heat improved time-trial performance and mitochondrial citrate synthase activity more than training in temperate conditions.

title: Efficacy of Vitamin D Supplementation in Addition to Aerobic Exercise Training in Obese Women with Perceived Myalgia: A Single-Blinded Randomized Controlled Clinical Trial
authors: Heba Ahmed Ali Abdeen, David Rodriguez-Sanz, Mahmoud Ewidea, Dina Mohamed Ali Al-Hamaky, Marwa Abd E...
abstract: This study examined vitamin D and aerobic exercise for obese women with muscle pain. Combining both treatments was most effective for reducing pain, improving vitamin D levels, and enhancing quality of life.

title: Influence of combined vitamin D 3  supplementation and resistance exercise training on musculoskeletal health in older men and women (EXVITD): protocol for a randomised controlled trial
authors: Anneka Elizabeth Welford, Susan Lanham-New, Janet Lord, Alison Doyle, Julie Robinson, Peter Nighting...
abstract: This randomized controlled trial investigates the effect of vitamin D3 supplementation combined with resistance exercise training on musculoskeletal health in older adults. The study aims to determine if this combination improves muscle function more than exercise training alone.

title: α -Tocopherol Protects the Heart, Muscles, and Testes from Lipid Peroxidation in Growing Male Rats Subjected to Physical Efforts
authors: Magdalena Górnicka, Anna Ciecierska, Jadwiga Hamulka, Małgorzata E. Drywień, Joanna Frackiewicz, Krz...
abstract: This study investigated the effects of training and α-tocopherol supplementation on tissue α-tocopherol and lipid peroxidation in male rats. Supplementation helped prevent exercise-induced lipid peroxidation in the heart, muscles, and testes.

title: α-Tocopherol Pharmacokinetics in Adults with Cystic Fibrosis: Benefits of Supplemental Vitamin C Administration
authors: Maret G. Traber, Scott W. Leonard, Vihas T. Vasu, Brian M. Morrissey, Huangshu (John) Lei, Jeffrey A...
abstract: This study investigated α-tocopherol pharmacokinetics in adults with cystic fibrosis, with and without vitamin C supplementation. Vitamin C administration slowed the plasma disappearance rate of α-tocopherol, suggesting it augments its concentration.

title: Effects of Peanut Protein Supplementation on Resistance Training Adaptations in Younger Adults
authors: Casey L. Sexton, Morgan A. Smith, Kristen S. Smith, Shelby C. Osburn, Joshua S. Godwin, Bradley A. R...
abstract: Peanut protein supplementation was studied alongside resistance training in young adults. The supplement did not affect muscle protein synthesis or strength gains in males and females.

title: Effects of Vitamin D3 Supplementation and Resistance Training on 25-Hydroxyvitamin D Status and Functional Performance of Older Adults: A Randomized Placebo-Controlled Trial
authors: Rudolf Aschauer, Sandra Unterberger, Patrick A. Zöhrer, Agnes Draxler, Bernhard Franzke, Eva-Maria S...
abstract: This study investigated the effects of vitamin D3 supplementation and resistance training on older adults. Vitamin D supplementation improved vitamin D status but did not enhance muscle performance or functional mobility beyond resistance training alone.

title: The effect of Vitamin E supplementation on treatment of chronic periodontitis
authors: Parichehr Behfarnia, Mina Dadmehr, Seyedeh Negin Hosseini, Seyed Amir Mirghaderi
abstract: This study investigated Vitamin E supplementation's effect on chronic periodontitis treatment. Vitamin E significantly reduced attachment loss compared to standard treatment alone.

title: Combined effect of high-dose vitamin A, vitamin E supplementation, and zinc on adult patients with diabetes: A randomized trial
authors: Eman Said, Shrook Mousa, May Fawzi, Nirmeen A. Sabry, Samar Farid
abstract: This randomized trial investigated the effects of vitamin A plus E supplementation, with and without zinc, on adult patients with type 2 diabetes. The combination of vitamins A and E with zinc significantly improved glycemic control and insulin secretion compared to a control group.

title: Adaptations to strength training differ between endurance-trained and untrained women
authors: Olav Vikmoen, Truls Raastad, Stian Ellefsen, Bent R. Rønnestad
abstract: Endurance-trained and untrained women underwent 11 weeks of strength training. Concurrent training did not impair strength or hypertrophy gains, but attenuated increases in explosive power.

title: A Dose-Dependent Effect of Carnipure ®  Tartrate Supplementation on Endurance Capacity, Recovery, and Body Composition in an Exercise Rat Model
authors: Kazim Sahin, Cemal Orhan, Osman Kucuk, Nurhan Sahin, Mehmet Tuzcu, Besir Er, Shane Durkee, Aouatef B...
abstract: Carnipure® Tartrate supplementation was studied in exercising rats to assess its effects on endurance, recovery, and body composition. The study found that CT supplementation dose-dependently improved endurance, recovery, and antioxidant capacity, while reducing body weight and fat.

title: The effects of isoflavone supplementation plus combined exercise on salivary markers of oxidative stress in postmenopausal women
authors: Ana Luiza Amaral, Anne M. Mendonça, Jéssica S. Giolo, Juliene G. Costa, Igor M. Mariano, Tállita C. ...
abstract: This study investigated isoflavone supplementation combined with exercise in postmenopausal women. Isoflavones, with exercise, reduced lipid peroxidation and salivary nitrite, suggesting an antioxidant effect.

title: Oral vitamin C restores endothelial function during acute inflammation in young and older adults
authors: Elizabeth C. Lefferts, Brooks A. Hibner, Wesley K. Lefferts, Natalia S. Lima, Tracy Baynard, Jacob M...
abstract: Oral vitamin C was given to young and older adults during acute inflammation to assess its effect on vascular function. Vitamin C restored endothelial function, but not aortic stiffness, during inflammation.

title: Does vitamin D supplementation improve bone health, body composition and physical performance beyond endurance exercise in patients with type 2 diabetes: A secondary analysis of randomized controlled trial
authors: Xiaomin Sun, Wenjuan Xiao, Zhongying Li, Sirui Zhou, Mengyue Dong, Cong Huang, Yan Ma, Bo Gou
abstract: This study examined the effects of vitamin D and endurance exercise on type 2 diabetes patients. Vitamin D supplementation alone did not improve outcomes beyond exercise, but it may help prevent exercise-induced bone loss.

title: Effect of Vitamin C and Protein Supplementation on Plasma Nitrate and Nitrite Response following Consumption of Beetroot Juice
authors: Gary D. Miller, Beverly A. Nesbit, Daniel B. Kim-Shapiro, Swati Basu, Michael J. Berry
abstract: This study investigated the effect of vitamin C or protein supplementation on plasma nitrate and nitrite levels after beetroot juice consumption. No significant differences were found in plasma nitrate and nitrite levels when beetroot juice was co-ingested with vitamin C or whey protein compared to beetroot juice alone.

title: Mangosteen Concentrate Drink Supplementation Promotes Antioxidant Status and Lactate Clearance in Rats after Exercise
authors: Ching-Chien Chang, Chia-Wen Chen, Eddy Owaga, Wan-Ting Lee, Ting-Ni Liu, Rong-Hong Hsieh
abstract: Mangosteen concentrate drink supplementation was studied in rats after running exercise. The drink increased antioxidant enzymes, reduced oxidative stress, and improved lactate clearance, benefiting muscle fatigue reduction.

title: The effect of vitamin E supplementation on selected inflammatory biomarkers in adults: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized clinical trials
authors: Omid Asbaghi, Mehdi Sadeghian, Behzad Nazarian, Mehrnoosh Sarreshtedari, Hassan Mozaffari-Khosravi, ...
abstract: This meta-analysis examined vitamin E's effects on inflammatory biomarkers in adults. Vitamin E, especially alpha-tocopherol, significantly reduced C-reactive protein and tumor necrosis factor-alpha levels.

title: Impact of protein supplementation during endurance training on changes in skeletal muscle transcriptome
authors: Pim Knuiman, Roland Hangelbroek, Mark Boekschoten, Maria Hopman, Marco Mensink
abstract: This study analyzed skeletal muscle transcriptome changes after endurance training with or without protein supplementation. Protein supplementation increased the number of differentially expressed genes, particularly those related to the extracellular matrix.

title: Biochemical and Clinical Effects of Vitamin E Supplementation in Hungarian Smith-Lemli-Opitz Syndrome Patients
authors: Katalin Koczok, László Horváth, Zeljka Korade, Zoltán András Mezei, Gabriella P. Szabó, Ned A. Porte...
abstract: This study investigated vitamin E supplementation in six SLOS patients already on cholesterol treatment. Vitamin E supplementation improved some behavioral and physical symptoms in half of the patients, particularly those with a lower baseline 7-DHC + 8-DHC/cholesterol ratio.

title: Dietary Adjustments to Altitude Training in Elite Endurance Athletes; Impact of a Randomized Clinical Trial With Antioxidant-Rich Foods
authors: Anu E. Koivisto-Mørk, Ingvild Paur, Gøran Paulsen, Ina Garthe, Truls Raastad, Nasser E. Bastani, Run...
source: Frontiers in Sports and Active Living
abstract: Elite endurance athletes increased energy, carbohydrate, iron, fluid, and antioxidant-rich food intake during altitude training. An antioxidant-rich snack intervention further boosted intake of specific nutrients but did not significantly alter blood parameters compared to a control group.

title: Alpha-Tocopherol Metabolites (The Vitamin E Metabolome) and Their Interindividual Variability during Supplementation
authors: Desirée Bartolini, Rita Marinelli, Danilo Giusepponi, Roberta Galarini, Carolina Barola, Anna Maria ...
abstract: This study analyzed vitamin E metabolites in healthy volunteers after supplementation. Metabolite levels showed significant interindividual variability, with some metabolites being poor indicators of intake, while others correlated with vitamin E levels and gene expression.

title: The effect of supplementation with vitamins A, B, C, D, and E on disease severity and inflammatory responses in patients with COVID-19: a randomized clinical trial
authors: Mohammad Taghi Beigmohammadi, Sama Bitarafan, Azin Hoseindokht, Alireza Abdollahi, Laya Amoozadeh, D...
abstract: This study investigated the impact of vitamin A, B, C, D, and E supplementation on COVID-19 patients in the ICU. Vitamin supplementation improved inflammatory markers and disease severity, but did not significantly affect mortality or prolonged hospitalization after adjustments.

title: Effects of exercise training and dietary supplement on fat free mass and bone mass density during weight loss – a systematic review and meta-analysis.
authors: Anja Roth, Martin Sattelmayer, Chloé Schorderet, Simone Gafner, Lara Allet, Nahid Ramezani-Jolfaie, ...
abstract: This systematic review and meta-analysis examined exercise training and dietary supplements' effects on fat-free mass during weight loss. Exercise training, particularly combined with high protein intake, significantly helps preserve fat-free mass.

title: Effects of Dietary Nitrate Supplementation on Performance and Muscle Oxygenation during Resistance Exercise in Men
authors: Rachel Tan, Adam Pennell, Katherine M. Price, Sean T. Karl, Noelle G. Seekamp-Hicks, Keonabelle K. P...
abstract: This study investigated beetroot juice supplementation's effects on resistance exercise performance and muscle oxygenation. Beetroot juice improved repetitions to failure in the bench press but had no effect on other performance measures or muscle oxygenation.

title: Effect of resistance training with and without vitamin D calcium chitosan nanoparticle supplements on apoptosis markers in ovariectomized rats: An experimental study
authors: Mahsa Dehghan-Manshadi, Mohammad-Ali Azarbayjani, Sirvan Atashak, Maghsoud Peeri, Saleh Rahmati-Ahma...
abstract: This study examined how resistance training and vitamin D/calcium/chitosan nanoparticles affect apoptosis markers in ovariectomized rats. The combination of resistance training and supplements appeared to reverse OVX-induced apoptosis.

title: The Relationship between Resistance Exercise Performance and Ventilatory Efficiency after Beetroot Juice Intake in Well-Trained Athletes
authors: Noemí Serra-Payá, Manuel Vicente Garnacho-Castaño, Sergio Sánchez-Nuño, Lluís Albesa-Albiol, Montser...
abstract: This study investigated the impact of beetroot juice on resistance exercise performance and ventilatory efficiency in athletes. Beetroot juice improved ventilatory efficiency and resistance exercise performance, suggesting an ergogenic effect under aerobic conditions.

title: On the effect of vitamin C intake on human health: How to (mis)interprete the clinical evidence
authors: Jens Lykkesfeldt
abstract: This review examines clinical studies on vitamin C's health effects beyond scurvy. It concludes that ignoring vitamin C's unique pharmacokinetics leads to flawed study designs and misinterpretation of results.

title: Performance and Submaximal Adaptations to Additional Speed-Endurance Training Vs. Continuous Moderate-Intensity Aerobic Training in Male Endurance Athletes
authors: Vincenzo Rago, Peter Krustrup, Magni Mohr
abstract: This study compared speed-endurance training (SET) with moderate-intensity training (MIT) in male endurance athletes. SET led to greater physiological demands and superior improvements in performance and running economy compared to MIT.

title: Oral vitamin C supplementation to patients with myeloid cancer on azacitidine treatment: Normalization of plasma vitamin C induces epigenetic changes
authors: Linn Gillberg, Andreas D. Ørskov, Ammar Nasif, Hitoshi Ohtani, Zachary Madaj, Jakob W. Hansen, Nicol...
abstract: This study investigated oral vitamin C supplementation in myeloid cancer patients treated with azacitidine. Normalizing plasma vitamin C levels increased the 5hmC/5mC ratio, suggesting enhanced DNMTi effects.

title: Exercise Performance Upregulatory Effect of R-α-Lipoic Acid with γ-Cyclodextrin
authors: Yuki Hashimoto, Katsuhiko Yoshizawa, Yuka Kaido, Akiko Takenouchi, Keiji Terao, Hiroyuki Yasui, Yuta...
abstract: This study investigated the effect of a γ-cyclodextrin complex of R-α-lipoic acid on exercise performance and oxidative stress in mice. The complex supplementation repressed exercise-induced blood ammonia elevation and reduced kidney oxidative stress, suggesting potential benefits for athletic performance.

title: Beetroot supplementation in women enjoying exercise together (BEE SWEET): Rationale, design and methods
authors: Marissa N. Baranauskas, Cody A. Altherr, Allison H. Gruber, Andrew R. Coggan, John S. Raglin, Samir ...
abstract: This study investigates if beetroot supplementation enhances exercise benefits in postmenopausal women. It aims to determine if beetroot juice improves mobility and cardiovascular health outcomes compared to exercise alone or exercise with a placebo.

title: High-dose testosterone supplementation disturbs liver pro-oxidant/antioxidant balance and function in adolescent male Wistar rats undergoing moderate-intensity endurance training
authors: Ewa Sadowska-Krępa, Barbara Kłapcińska, Anna Nowara, Sławomir Jagsz, Izabela Szołtysek-Bołdys, Małgo...
abstract: High-dose testosterone supplementation was studied in adolescent rats undergoing endurance training. It disrupted the liver's antioxidant balance and function, increasing oxidative stress markers and enzyme activities.

title: Vitamin C Is Essential for the Maintenance of Skeletal Muscle Functions
authors: Shoko Takisawa, Yuka Takino, Jaewon Lee, Shuichi Machida, Akihito Ishigami
abstract: Long-term vitamin C deficiency was studied in male mice lacking VC synthesis, showing muscle atrophy and reduced physical ability. Vitamin C is essential for maintaining skeletal muscle function in both sexes.

title: Association of vitamin E intake in diet and supplements with risk of dementia: A meta-analysis
authors: Rangyin Zhao, Xiaoyong Han, Hongxia Zhang, Jia Liu, Min Zhang, Weijing Zhao, Shangrong Jiang, Ruilin...
abstract: This meta-analysis examined the relationship between vitamin E intake and dementia risk. High vitamin E intake, from both diet and supplements, was found to significantly reduce the risk of dementia and Alzheimer's disease.

title: Effect of Vitamin E Supplementation on Deposition and Gene Expression Profiling of Abdominal Fat in Broiler Chickens
authors: Min Zhang, Jianlei Li, Yuting Zhu, Qiong Wu, Yan Li, Dingrui Huang, Zhending Gan, Lipeng Zhong, Jing...
abstract: This study investigated vitamin E's effect on broiler abdominal fat deposition and gene expression. Vitamin E supplementation reduced fat deposition and altered genes involved in fatty acid biosynthesis and lipid metabolism.

title: Circulating nitrate-nitrite reduces oxygen uptake for improving resistance exercise performance after rest time in well-trained CrossFit athletes
authors: Manuel Vicente Garnacho-Castaño, Sergio Sánchez-Nuño, Lorena Molina-Raya, Teresa Carbonell, José Lui...
abstract: Circulating nitrate-nitrite from beetroot juice was studied in CrossFit athletes performing resistance exercise. Higher NOx reduced oxygen uptake during rest, improving squat performance.

title: Effects of electrotactic exercise and antioxidant EUK-134 on oxidative stress relief in  Caenorhabditis elegans
authors: Thi Thanh Huong Pham, Wan-Ying Huang, Chang-Shi Chen, Wen-Tai Chiu, Han-Sheng Chuang
abstract: Electrotactic exercise and antioxidant EUK-134 were studied for their effects on oxidative stress in *C. elegans*. The combination significantly improved worm survivorship, reproduction, and motility, suggesting long-term antioxidative stress benefits.

title: Vitamin C—Sources, Physiological Role, Kinetics, Deficiency, Use, Toxicity, and Determination
authors: Martin Doseděl, Eduard Jirkovský, Kateřina Macáková, Lenka Kujovská Krčmová, Lenka Javorská, Jana Po...
abstract: This review discusses vitamin C's broad physiological roles beyond its antioxidant function, including its impact on iron absorption and epigenetic processes. While essential for preventing scurvy, high doses can be pro-oxidant and potentially harmful, with limited proven benefits for other diseases.

title: The Effect of Beta-Alanine versus Alkaline Agent Supplementation Combined with Branched-Chain Amino Acids and Creatine Malate in Highly-Trained Sprinters and Endurance Athletes: A Randomized Double-Blind Crossover Study
authors: Krzysztof Durkalec-Michalski, Krzysztof Kusy, Monika Ciekot-Sołtysiak, Jacek Zieliński
abstract: This study investigated the effects of beta-alanine versus alkaline agents, combined with BCAAs and creatine malate, on elite sprinters and endurance athletes. Beta-alanine supplementation led to increased fat-free mass in sprinters and reduced post-exercise ammonia in both groups, but did not improve aerobic capacity.

title: Acute Beetroot Juice Supplementation Enhances Intermittent Running Performance but Does Not Reduce Oxygen Cost of Exercise among Recreational Adults
authors: Ozcan Esen, Raúl Domínguez, Raci Karayigit
abstract: Acute beetroot juice supplementation was studied for its effects on intermittent running performance and oxygen cost. It improved performance but did not reduce oxygen consumption in recreational adults.

title: Effects of Exercise Combined with Undenatured Type II Collagen on Endurance Capacity, Antioxidant Status, Muscle Lipogenic Genes and E3 Ubiquitin Ligases in Rats
authors: Cemal Orhan, Emre Sahin, Besir Er, Mehmet Tuzcu, Andrey P. Lopes, Nurhan Sahin, Vijaya Juturu, Kazim...
abstract: Exercise combined with undenatured type II collagen improved endurance capacity and antioxidant status in rats. It also reduced muscle lipogenic gene expression and markers of muscle damage.

title: Changes in Oxidative Stress, Inflammation, and Muscle Damage Markers Following Diet and Beetroot Juice Supplementation in Elite Fencers
authors: Lucyna Kozłowska, Olga Mizera, Jolanta Gromadzińska, Beata Janasik, Karolina Mikołajewska, Anna Mróz...
abstract: This study examined the effects of dietary recommendations and beetroot juice supplementation on elite fencers. Beetroot juice supplementation increased VO2max, which was linked to changes in muscle damage and oxidative stress markers.

title: Beetroot Juice Produces Changes in Heart Rate Variability and Reduces Internal Load during Resistance Training in Men: A Randomized Double-Blind Crossover
authors: Jose Manuel Jurado-Castro, David Casanova-Rodriguez, Julian Campos-Perez, Francisco Jesus Llorente-C...
abstract: This study investigated the effects of beetroot juice supplementation on autonomic nervous system responses during resistance training. Beetroot juice reduced internal training load and altered heart rate variability during exercise compared to a placebo.

title: Four months vitamin D supplementation to vitamin D insufficient individuals does not improve muscular strength: A randomized controlled trial
authors: Guri Grimnes, Julia Kubiak, Rolf Jorde
abstract: This study investigated the effect of vitamin D supplementation on muscle strength in vitamin D insufficient individuals. Four months of supplementation did not improve muscle strength compared to placebo.

title: Acute Beetroot Juice Supplementation Attenuates Morning-Associated Decrements in Supramaximal Exercise Performance in Trained Sprinters
authors: Amanda M. Dumar, Anna F. Huntington, Rebecca R. Rogers, Thomas J. Kopec, Tyler D. Williams, Christop...
source: International Journal of Environmental Research and Public Health
abstract: This study investigated the effect of beetroot juice on morning exercise performance in sprinters. Beetroot juice supplementation prevented the typical morning performance decrements observed in trained sprinters.

title: Oral Arginine Supplementation in Healthy Individuals Performing Regular Resistance Training
authors: Ștefan-Sebastian Busnatu, Octavian Andronic, Maria-Alexandra Pană, Anca Pantea Stoian, Alexandru Sca...
abstract: Oral arginine supplementation was studied in healthy men performing resistance training. Arginine supplementation reduced blood pressure and improved body composition compared to a control group.

title: Vitamin C for Cardiac Protection during Percutaneous Coronary Intervention: A Systematic Review of Randomized Controlled Trials
authors: Sher Ali Khan, Sandipan Bhattacharjee, Muhammad Owais Abdul Ghani, Rachel Walden, Qin M. Chen
abstract: This systematic review analyzed eight randomized controlled trials on vitamin C's effect on cardiac protection during percutaneous coronary intervention. Vitamin C administration before PCI was found to reduce cardiac injury markers and inflammation.

title: Muscle-Related Effect of Whey Protein and Vitamin D 3  Supplementation Provided before or after Bedtime in Males Undergoing Resistance Training
authors: Yan Chen, Yiheng Liang, Hang Guo, Kun Meng, Junqiang Qiu, Dan Benardot
abstract: This study examined the effects of whey protein and vitamin D supplementation before or after sleep on muscle mass and strength during resistance training. Both supplementation timings led to significant improvements in muscle mass and hormones compared to a placebo.

title: Effects of dietary supplementation of vitamin-E and commercial probiotics on the innate immunity of  Labeo rohita  against  Aeromonas hydrophila  infection
authors: Leesa Priyadarsani, Thangapalam Jawahar Abraham, Harresh Adikesavalu, Gadadhar Dash, Talagunda Srini...
abstract: This study investigated the effects of vitamin E and probiotics on the innate immunity of Labeo rohita against Aeromonas hydrophila. Both supplements enhanced immunity, with vitamin E at 100 mg/kg proving more effective than probiotics at 5 g/kg.

title: Prolonged Heat Acclimation and Aerobic Performance in Endurance Trained Athletes
authors: C. Jacob Mikkelsen, Nicklas Junge, Jacob F. Piil, Nathan B. Morris, Laura Oberholzer, Christoph Sieb...
abstract: This study investigated prolonged heat acclimation's effects on endurance cyclists' aerobic performance in cool conditions. Prolonged heat training did not improve aerobic power or time trial performance in cool weather compared to standard training.

title: Acute Effects of Beetroot Juice Supplements on Resistance Training: A Randomized Double-Blind Crossover
authors: Antonio Ranchal-Sanchez, Victor Manuel Diaz-Bernier, Candelaria Alonso De La Florida-Villagran, Fran...
abstract: This study examined beetroot juice's effects on resistance training performance. Beetroot juice supplementation increased the total number of repetitions performed during resistance training.

title: Nicotinic Acid Improves Endurance Performance of Mice Subjected to Treadmill Exercise
authors: Robert Ringseis, Denise K. Gessner, Anna M. Beer, Yvonne Albrecht, Gaiping Wen, Erika Most, Karsten ...
abstract: This study investigated the effect of a high nicotinic acid diet combined with treadmill exercise on mouse endurance performance. The combined treatment significantly improved endurance and altered muscle fiber composition compared to exercise alone or control.

title: Dose Response of Acute ATP Supplementation on Strength Training Performance
authors: Helton Pereira dos Santos Nunes de Moura, Ralf Jäger, Martin Purpura, John A. Rathmacher, John C. Fu...
source: Frontiers in Sports and Active Living
abstract: This study investigated the dose response of acute oral ATP supplementation on strength training performance. A 400 mg dose of ATP significantly increased repetitions, while 100 mg reduced perceived exertion.

title: Effect of whey vs. soy protein supplementation on recovery kinetics following speed endurance training in competitive male soccer players: a randomized controlled trial
authors: Savvas Kritikos, Konstantinos Papanikolaou, Dimitrios Draganidis, Athanasios Poulios, Kalliopi Georg...
source: Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition
abstract: Whey and soy protein supplementation were studied for their effects on recovery after soccer speed-endurance training. Neither protein source improved performance or muscle damage markers compared to placebo.

title: The effects of resistance training with or without peanut protein supplementation on skeletal muscle and strength adaptations in older individuals
authors: Donald A. Lamb, Johnathon H. Moore, Morgan A. Smith, Christopher G. Vann, Shelby C. Osburn, Bradley ...
source: Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition
abstract: This study investigated the effects of resistance training with or without peanut protein supplementation on muscle and strength in older adults. Peanut protein supplementation showed some benefits in muscle thickness and strength, but not overall body composition or acute muscle protein synthesis.

title: Lung Function and Respiratory Muscle Adaptations of Endurance- and Strength-Trained Males
authors: Daniel A. Hackett
abstract: This study compared lung function and respiratory muscle strength in endurance-trained versus strength-trained males. Endurance trainers showed greater maximal voluntary ventilation, while strength trainers had greater respiratory muscle strength, which was linked to lower body strength.

title: Right heart exercise-training-adaptation and remodelling in endurance athletes
authors: Valeria Conti, Filippo Migliorini, Marco Pilone, María I. Barriopedro, Juan José Ramos-Álvarez, Fran...
abstract: This systematic review examined right heart structural and functional changes in endurance athletes. Findings indicate that right heart remodeling in athletes is associated with age, body surface area, and training intensity.

title: Sustained Endurance Training Leads to Metabolomic Adaptation
authors: Astrid Weiss, Katharina Alack, Stephan Klatt, Sven Zukunft, Ralph Schermuly, Torsten Frech, Frank-Ch...
abstract: This study compared the metabolomic profiles of endurance-trained and untrained individuals. Endurance training leads to distinct changes in phospholipids, acylcarnitines, bile acids, and polyunsaturated fatty acids at rest.

title: Effect of milk fat globule membrane supplementation on motor unit adaptation following resistance training in older adults
authors: Kohei Watanabe, Aleš Holobar, Aya Tomita, Yukiko Mita
abstract: This study examined the effect of milk fat globule membrane (MFGM) supplementation on motor unit adaptation during resistance training in older adults. MFGM supplementation maintained higher motor unit firing rates and altered firing patterns compared to placebo.

title: Acute beetroot juice supplementation improves exercise tolerance and cycling efficiency in adults with obesity
authors: Christian E. Behrens, Khandaker Ahmed, Karina Ricart, Braxton Linder, José Fernández, Brenda Bertran...
abstract: This study investigated the effects of beetroot juice on exercise in adults with obesity. Beetroot juice improved exercise efficiency and tolerance compared to other conditions.

title: Melatonin Supplement Plus Exercise Effectively Counteracts the Challenges of Isoproterenol-Induced Cardiac Injury in Rats
authors: Md. Mahbubur Rahman, Dong Kwon Yang
abstract: This study investigated the combined effects of exercise and melatonin on isoproterenol-induced cardiac injury in rats. The combination treatment effectively counteracted cardiac injury by preserving mitochondrial function and reducing oxidative stress.

title: Antioxidant trials—the need to test for stress
authors: Robert John Aitken

title: The Effect of Beetroot Ingestion on High-Intensity Interval Training: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
authors: Tak Hiong Wong, Alexiaa Sim, Stephen F. Burns
abstract: This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated beetroot supplementation's effects on high-intensity interval training performance. Beetroot supplementation showed no significant improvement in peak or mean power output during HIIT or SIT.

title: Lower Dietary and Circulating Vitamin C in Middle- and Older-Aged Men and Women Are Associated with Lower Estimated Skeletal Muscle Mass
authors: Lucy N Lewis, Richard P G Hayhoe, Angela A Mulligan, Robert N Luben, Kay-Tee Khaw, Ailsa A Welch
abstract: This study examined the relationship between vitamin C intake and levels with skeletal muscle mass in middle-aged and older adults. Lower dietary and circulating vitamin C were associated with lower estimated skeletal muscle mass.

title: Neither Beetroot Juice Supplementation nor Increased Carbohydrate Oxidation Enhance Economy of Prolonged Exercise in Elite Race Walkers
authors: Louise M. Burke, Rebecca Hall, Ida A. Heikura, Megan L. Ross, Nicolin Tee, Georgina L. Kent, Jamie W...
abstract: Beetroot juice and increased carbohydrate availability strategies were tested in elite race walkers. Neither approach improved exercise economy or substrate oxidation rates.

title: Effects of Endurance and Endurance–Strength Training on Endothelial Function in Women with Obesity: A Randomized Trial
authors: Marzena Ratajczak, Damian Skrypnik, Paweł Bogdański, Edyta Mądry, Jarosław Walkowiak, Monika Szulińs...
source: International Journal of Environmental Research and Public Health
abstract: This study compared endurance and combined endurance-strength training in obese women. Endurance training alone improved endothelial function markers, while both improved lipid metabolism.

title: Vitamin C supplementation promotes mental vitality in healthy young adults: results from a cross-sectional analysis and a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial
authors: Minju Sim, Sehwa Hong, Sungwoong Jung, Jin-Soo Kim, Young-Tae Goo, Woo Young Chun, Dong-Mi Shin
abstract: A cross-sectional study and RCT examined vitamin C's link to mental vitality. Vitamin C supplementation improved attention and work absorption in young adults with inadequate levels.

title: KiwiC for Vitality: Results of a Placebo-Controlled Trial Testing the Effects of Kiwifruit or Vitamin C Tablets on Vitality in Adults with Low Vitamin C Levels
authors: Tamlin S. Conner, Benjamin D. Fletcher, Jillian J. Haszard, Juliet M. Pullar, Emma Spencer, Louise A...
abstract: This study tested kiwifruit and vitamin C on vitality in adults with low vitamin C. Both kiwifruit and vitamin C improved well-being, with kiwifruit also reducing fatigue and improving mood.

title: Antioxidant Supplements and Oxidative Stress
authors: Jumana Saleh, Marvin Edeas, Harry Van Goor

title: Understanding the effects of beetroot juice intake on CrossFit performance by assessing hormonal, metabolic and mechanical response: a randomized, double-blind, crossover design
authors: Manuel Vicente Garnacho-Castaño, Guillem Palau-Salvà, Noemí Serra-Payá, Mario Ruiz-Hermosel, Marina ...
abstract: This study investigated the effects of beetroot juice on CrossFit performance, measuring hormonal, metabolic, and mechanical responses. Beetroot juice improved performance when rest was provided between exercises, but increased cortisol, reduced oxygen saturation, and heightened muscular fatigue.

title: Differences in Training Adaptations of Endurance Performance during Combined Strength and Endurance Training in a 6-Month Crisis Management Operation
authors: Kai Pihlainen, Keijo Häkkinen, Matti Santtila, Jani Raitanen, Heikki Kyröläinen
source: International Journal of Environmental Research and Public Health
abstract: This study compared training adaptations in soldiers during a 6-month operation. Soldiers who were initially leaner and fitter were more likely to experience a decrease in aerobic fitness.

title: Vitamin D supplementation and increased dairy protein intake do not affect muscle strength or physical function in healthy 6–8-year-old children: the  D-pro  randomized trial
authors: Line Thams, Lars G. Hvid, Nanna G. Stounbjerg, Jan C. Brønd, Christian Mølgaard, Camilla T. Damsgaar...
abstract: This study investigated vitamin D and increased dairy protein intake's effects on children's muscle strength and physical function. Neither intervention, alone or combined, improved these measures in healthy children.

title: Effect of an Antioxidant Supplement Combination on Boar Sperm
authors: Ivan Galić, Saša Dragin, Ivan Stančić, Milan Maletić, Jelena Apić, Nebojša Kladar, Jovan Spasojević,...
abstract: This study investigated the effect of an antioxidant supplement combination on boar seminal plasma and sperm quality. The supplements improved sperm DNA integrity and motility, despite no significant changes in total antioxidant capacity or glutathione peroxidase.

title: Effects of Beetroot Juice Supplementation on Cognitive Function, Aerobic and Anaerobic Performances of Trained Male Taekwondo Athletes: A Pilot Study
authors: Hossein Miraftabi, Zahra Avazpoor, Erfan Berjisian, Amir Sarshin, Sajjad Rezaei, Raúl Domínguez, Rei...
source: International Journal of Environmental Research and Public Health
abstract: This pilot study examined the effects of two doses of beetroot juice on taekwondo athletes' performance and cognitive function. The 400 mg dose of beetroot juice improved cognitive function after a performance test, though no significant performance differences were found.

title: Acute Effects of Beetroot Juice Supplementation on Isometric Muscle Strength, Rate of Torque Development and Isometric Endurance in Young Adult Men and Women: A Randomized, Double-Blind, Controlled Cross-Over Pilot Study
authors: David Poredoš, Zala Jenko Pražnikar, Žiga Kozinc
abstract: This study examined beetroot juice's effects on isometric strength and endurance in young adults. Beetroot juice did not improve maximal strength but enhanced endurance and torque development rate in men, not women.

title: Effects of antioxidant supplement on immune health and physical wellbeing: A randomized, controlled trial
authors: Jessie Hawkins, Christy Hires, Elizabeth Dunne, Lindsey Keenan
abstract: An antioxidant supplement was tested against a placebo in healthy adults. The supplement significantly improved overall health, reduced illness duration, and enhanced sleep quality.

title: Estimation of Vitamin C Intake Requirements Based on Body Weight: Implications for Obesity
authors: Anitra C. Carr, Gladys Block, Jens Lykkesfeldt
abstract: This study estimated vitamin C intake needs based on body weight. Higher body weight requires more vitamin C to maintain comparable plasma levels, suggesting current recommendations may be insufficient for heavier individuals.

title: Reply: antioxidant trials—the need to test for stress
authors: Mohan S Kamath, Mariano Mascarenhas, Treasa Joseph, Muthukumar Karthikeyan, Aleyamma T Kunjummen

title: l -Arginine and Beetroot Extract Supplementation in the Prevention of Sarcopenia
authors: Alfredo Córdova-Martínez, Alberto Caballero-García, Hugo J. Bello, Antoni Pons-Biescas, David C. Nor...
abstract: This study investigated the effects of l-arginine and beetroot extract supplementation on muscle function in older adults over six weeks. Beetroot extract showed some benefits for women's muscle functionality and men's sprint performance, while l-arginine had no significant impact.

title: Vitamin C and COVID-19
authors: Harri Hemilä, Angelique M. E. de Man
abstract: This paper reviews vitamin C's potential benefits for viral infections, particularly in critically ill patients. Findings suggest vitamin C may reduce ICU stays, mechanical ventilation duration, and mortality in sepsis patients.

title: Immunoregulatory effects of testosterone supplementation combined with exercise training in men with Inclusion Body Myositis: a double‐blind, placebo‐controlled, cross‐over trial
authors: Jerome D Coudert, Nataliya Slater, Anuradha Sooda, Kelly Beer, Ee Mun Lim, Conchita Boyder, Rui Zhan...
abstract: This study investigated the effects of testosterone supplementation combined with exercise in men with Inclusion Body Myositis. Exercise alone reduced inflammatory markers, with testosterone providing some additional immune changes.

title: Vitamin C for COVID-19 Treatment: Have We Got Enough Evidence?
authors: Siti Rohaiza Ahmad

title: Effect of beetroot or beetroot plus vitamin C supplementation on cardiovascular function in patients with coronary artery disease: protocol for a double-blind, placebo-controlled, randomised trial
authors: Leila Sadat Bahrami, Mohsen Mohebaty, Seyyed Mostafa Arabi, Hamed Tabesh, Mohsen Nematy, Reza Rezvan...
abstract: This study investigates the effects of beetroot and beetroot plus vitamin C supplementation on cardiovascular function in patients with coronary artery disease. The trial will assess changes in various cardiovascular markers over four weeks of supplementation.

title: Evaluating Vitamin C in Septic Shock: A Randomized Controlled Trial of Vitamin C Monotherapy*
authors: David A. Wacker, Susan L. Burton, John P. Berger, A. J. Hegg, Jamie Heisdorffer, Qi Wang, Emily J. M...
abstract: A randomized controlled trial evaluated IV vitamin C monotherapy in septic shock patients. Vitamin C did not significantly reduce 28-day mortality, and its routine clinical use is not supported.

title: Resistance Training Improves Muscle Strength and Function, Regardless of Protein Supplementation, in the Mid- to Long-Term Period after Gastric Bypass
authors: Gabriela S. Oliveira, Flávio T. Vieira, Fernando Lamarca, Ricardo M. Lima, Kênia M. B. Carvalho, Eli...
abstract: Resistance training was studied in individuals 2-7 years post-gastric bypass, with or without protein supplementation. Resistance training alone, or with protein, improved muscle strength and physical function.

title: Does Acute Beetroot Juice Supplementation Improve Neuromuscular Performance and Match Activity in Young Basketball Players? A Randomized, Placebo-Controlled Study
authors: Álvaro López-Samanes, Aarón Gómez Parra, Victor Moreno-Pérez, Javier Courel-Ibáñez
abstract: This study investigated acute beetroot juice supplementation's effects on young basketball players' neuromuscular performance and match activity. No significant improvements were found in jump height, strength, sprint, agility, or physical match demands.

title: Effect of  Nigella sativa  Supplementation on Oxidative Stress and Antioxidant Parameters: A Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials
authors: M. Ardiana, B. S. Pikir, A. Santoso, H. O. Hermawan, M. J. Al-Farabi
abstract: This meta-analysis examined the effect of Nigella sativa supplementation on oxidative stress. Nigella sativa supplementation increased superoxide dismutase levels but did not significantly affect malondialdehyde or total antioxidant capacity.

title: Effects of Running-Specific Strength Training, Endurance Training, and Concurrent Training on Recreational Endurance Athletes’ Performance and Selected Anthropometric Parameters
authors: Pablo Prieto-González, Jaromir Sedlacek
abstract: This study investigated the effects of running-specific strength, endurance, and concurrent training on recreational runners. Concurrent training demonstrated the most comprehensive improvements in body composition and performance metrics.

title: Effect of vitamin D supplementation on brain waves, behavioral performance, nitric oxide, malondialdehyde, and high-sensitivity C-reactive protein in children with attention deficit/hyperactivity disorder: study protocol for a randomized clinical trial
authors: Abbas Ali Sangouni, Hamid Mirhosseini, Mahdieh Hosseinzadeh
abstract: This study protocol outlines a randomized clinical trial investigating vitamin D supplementation in children with ADHD. It aims to assess the impact on brain waves, behavior, and specific biomarkers.

title: Vitamin D Supplementation Improves Handgrip Strength in Postmenopausal Women: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials
authors: Jia-Li Zhang, Christina Chui-Wa Poon, Man-Sau Wong, Wen-Xiong Li, Yi-Xun Guo, Yan Zhang
abstract: This systematic review and meta-analysis examined randomized controlled trials on vitamin D supplementation and muscle function in postmenopausal women. Vitamin D supplementation significantly improved handgrip strength, indicating enhanced muscle strength.

title: Isolated Soy Protein Supplementation Combined With Resistance Training Improves Muscle Strength, Mass, and Physical Performance of Aging Female Mice
authors: Mon-Chien Lee, Yi-Ju Hsu, Fang-Yu Wu, Chi-Chang Huang, Hsueh-Yu Li, Wen-Chyuan Chen
abstract: Isolated soy protein and resistance training were studied in aging female mice. Combining both interventions significantly improved muscle strength, mass, and physical performance.

title: VITADIAL “Does correction of 25 OH-VITAmin D with cholecalciferol supplementation increase muscle strength in hemoDIALysis patients?”: study protocol for a randomized controlled trial
authors: Stanislas Bataille, Nathalie Pedinielli, Elisa Carreno, Mathilde Prezelin-Reydit, Philippe Chauveau,...
abstract: This study protocol outlines a randomized controlled trial investigating if cholecalciferol supplementation improves muscle strength in hemodialysis patients with low vitamin D. The primary finding will be whether this supplementation leads to increased muscle strength over six months.

title: Supplements of an aqueous combination of  Justicia adhatoda  and  Ocimum tenuiflorum  boost antioxidative effects and impede hyperlipidemia
