authors: Ifrahim Iqbal Chowdhury, Md. Atiar Rahman, Mohammad A. Hashem, M. Mosharef Hossain Bhuiyan, Dina Haj...
abstract: This study investigated the combined effects of *Justicia adhatoda* and *Ocimum tenuiflorum* extracts on hyperlipidemia and oxidative stress in rats. The combination extract significantly improved lipid profiles, reduced atherogenic index, and enhanced antioxidative capacity.

title: Six Sessions of Sprint-Interval Training Did Not Improve Endurance and Neuromuscular Performance in Untrained Men
authors: Raphael Bertschinger, Louis-Solal Giboin, Markus Gruber
abstract: Six sessions of sprint-interval training were administered to untrained men to assess endurance and neuromuscular performance. The training did not improve endurance or neuromuscular function compared to a control group.

title: Nitrate-rich beetroot juice offsets salivary acidity following carbohydrate ingestion before and after endurance exercise in healthy male runners
authors: Mia C. Burleigh, Nicholas Sculthorpe, Fiona L. Henriquez, Chris Easton
abstract: Nitrate-rich beetroot juice was studied for its effect on salivary pH in male runners after carbohydrate ingestion and exercise. Ingesting nitrate attenuated the expected reduction in salivary pH, suggesting a potential oral health benefit for athletes.

title: Adaptation mechanism of the adult zebrafish respiratory organ to endurance training
authors: Matthias Messerli, Dea Aaldijk, David Haberthür, Helena Röss, Carolina García-Poyatos, Marcos Sande-...
abstract: Adult zebrafish underwent endurance training to study respiratory adaptation. The trained fish showed increased gill volume and filament growth, enhancing oxygen uptake.

title: Supplementation with Resveratrol, Piperine and Alpha-Tocopherol Decreases Chronic Inflammation in a Cluster of Older Adults with Metabolic Syndrome
authors: Raúl Francisco Pastor, Marisa Gabriela Repetto, Fabiana Lairion, Alberto Lazarowski, Amalia Merelli,...
abstract: A supplement of resveratrol, piperine, and alpha-tocopherol was tested in older adults with metabolic syndrome. The supplement significantly reduced markers of chronic inflammation and oxidative stress.

title: Influence of Interval Training Frequency on Time-Trial Performance in Elite Endurance Athletes
authors: Espen Tønnessen, Jonny Hisdal, Bent R. Ronnestad
abstract: This study compared the effects of four short versus two longer interval training sessions weekly in elite endurance athletes. Two longer sessions per week led to greater improvements in time-trial performance and physiological adaptations than four shorter sessions.

title: Mindfulness Training Enhances Endurance Performance and Executive Functions in Athletes: An Event-Related Potential Study
authors: Jui-Ti Nien, Chih-Han Wu, Kao-Teng Yang, Yu-Min Cho, Chien-Heng Chu, Yu-Kai Chang, Chenglin Zhou
abstract: A five-week mindfulness program was tested on university athletes. The training improved endurance, executive functions, and reduced neural conflict monitoring.

title: No Significant Differences in Muscle Growth and Strength Development When Consuming Soy and Whey Protein Supplements Matched for Leucine Following a 12 Week Resistance Training Program in Men and Women: A Randomized Trial
authors: Heidi M. Lynch, Matthew P. Buman, Jared M. Dickinson, Lynda B. Ransdell, Carol S. Johnston, Christop...
abstract: This study compared soy and whey protein supplements matched for leucine in untrained individuals undergoing resistance training. No significant differences in muscle growth or strength development were found between the two protein groups.

title: Effects of beetroot juice intake on repeated performance of competitive swimmers
authors: Berta Moreno, Esther Morencos, Davinia Vicente-Campos, Alejandro Muñoz, Jaime González-García, Santi...
abstract: Competitive swimmers were studied for the effects of beetroot juice on repeated maximal effort swimming. Beetroot juice did not significantly improve overall performance, but showed a trend towards better recovery and fatigue tolerance.

title: Effects of Beetroot Juice Ingestion on Physical Performance in Highly Competitive Tennis Players
authors: Álvaro López-Samanes, Alberto Pérez-López, Victor Moreno-Pérez, Fabio Yuzo Nakamura, Jorge Acebes-Sá...
abstract: This study investigated the effects of beetroot juice on tennis players' physical performance. Beetroot juice consumption did not significantly improve serve velocity, jumping, grip strength, agility, or sprinting in these athletes.

title: Intravenous vitamin C administration to patients with septic shock: a pilot randomised controlled trial
authors: Patrice Rosengrave, Emma Spencer, Jonathan Williman, Jan Mehrtens, Stacey Morgan, Tara Doyle, Kymbal...
abstract: A pilot randomized controlled trial investigated intravenous vitamin C in septic shock patients. Vitamin C administration did not significantly reduce vasopressor requirements or improve other clinical outcomes compared to placebo.

title: Beetroot juice — a suitable post-marathon metabolic recovery supplement?
authors: Zinandré Stander, Laneke Luies, Mari van Reenen, Glyn Howatson, Karen M. Keane, Tom Clifford, Emma J...
source: Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition
abstract: This study analyzed marathon runners' metabolic recovery after beetroot juice supplementation. Beetroot juice did not significantly alter overall metabolic recovery compared to a placebo, but influenced specific carbohydrate and fatty acid metabolites.

title: Lessening Organ dysfunction with VITamin C (LOVIT): protocol for a randomized controlled trial
authors: Marie-Hélène Masse, Julie Ménard, Sheila Sprague, Marie-Claude Battista, Deborah J. Cook, Gordon H. ...
abstract: This study is a randomized controlled trial investigating the effect of intravenous vitamin C on sepsis outcomes. It aims to determine if vitamin C reduces death or persistent organ dysfunction at 28 days.

title: Performance-Related Physiological and Haematological Changes During Pregnancy and Postpartum in a Well-Trained Cyclist Performing Endurance Training
authors: Nicki Winfield Almquist, Øyvind Sandbakk, Guro Strøm Solli
abstract: This case study tracked physiological and hematological changes in a trained cyclist during pregnancy and postpartum. Hematological values increased during pregnancy without a corresponding VO2peak rise, but training helped restore VO2peak and improve power postpartum.

title: Pharmacokinetics of Nitrate and Nitrite Following Beetroot Juice Drink Consumption
authors: Emily Margaret Jakubcik, Kay Rutherfurd-Markwick, Marsanne Chabert, Marie Wong, Ajmol Ali
abstract: This study investigated the effects of different nitrate and nitrite levels from beetroot juice on cardiovascular measures. Both nitrate and nitrite from beetroot juice can lower mean arterial pressure, but their impact on blood pressure reduction is unclear.

title: Early administration of Vitamin C in patients with sepsis or septic shock in emergency departments: A multicenter, double blinded, randomized controlled trial: The C-EASIE trial protocol
authors: Stefanie Vandervelden, Lina Wauters, Jan Breuls, Steffen Fieuws, Philippe Vanhove, Ives Hubloue, Mag...
abstract: This study is a randomized controlled trial investigating the early administration of Vitamin C in sepsis patients. It aims to determine if this intervention improves outcomes like shock resolution and reduces morbidity and mortality.

title: Incremental Doses of Nitrate-Rich Beetroot Juice Do Not Modify Cognitive Function and Cerebral Blood Flow in Overweight and Obese Older Adults: A 13-Week Pilot Randomised Clinical Trial
authors: Abrar M. Babateen, Oliver M. Shannon, Gerard M. O’Brien, Edward Okello, Ellen Smith, Dilara Olgacer,...
abstract: This pilot study investigated the effects of beetroot juice on cognitive function and cerebral blood flow in overweight and obese older adults over 13 weeks. No significant changes were observed in cognitive function or cerebral blood flow across different beetroot juice doses.

title: Multi-Fold Enhancement of Tocopherol Yields Employing High CO 2  Supplementation and Nitrate Limitation in Native Isolate  Monoraphidium  sp.
authors: Rabinder Singh, Asha Arumugam Nesamma, Alka Narula, Pannaga Pavan Jutur
abstract: High CO2 supplementation and nitrate limitation were employed to enhance tocopherol yields in *Monoraphidium* sp. This combination resulted in a multi-fold increase in tocopherol production, biomass, and lipids.

title: Acceptability and Feasibility of a 13-Week Pilot Randomised Controlled Trial Testing the Effects of Incremental Doses of Beetroot Juice in Overweight and Obese Older Adults
authors: Abrar M. Babateen, Oliver M. Shannon, Gerard M. O’Brien, Edward Okello, Anmar A. Khan, Sofia Rubele,...
abstract: A pilot RCT tested beetroot juice doses in overweight, obese older adults for 13 weeks. Prolonged beetroot juice supplementation is feasible in this population, with dose-dependent increases in nitrate levels.

title: An Untargeted Metabolomics Approach to Investigate the Metabolic Effect of Beetroot Juice Supplementation in Fencers—A Preliminary Study
authors: Lucyna Kozlowska, Olga Mizera, Anna Mroz
abstract: This study used untargeted metabolomics to analyze fencers' urine after beetroot juice supplementation. Beetroot juice significantly altered tyrosine and tryptophan metabolism, impacting neurotransmitter pathways.

title: No effect of nitrate-rich beetroot juice on microvascular function and blood pressure in younger and older individuals: a randomised, placebo-controlled double-blind pilot study
authors: David Rogerson, Fabio Alejandro Aguilar Mora, Jamie Stuart Young, Markos Klonizakis
abstract: This pilot study investigated nitrate-rich beetroot juice's impact on microvascular function and blood pressure in younger and older adults. No significant effects were observed on either parameter in either age group.

title: Metabolomic analysis of serum alpha-tocopherol among men in the Alpha-Tocopherol, Beta-Carotene Cancer Prevention (ATBC) Study
authors: Wayne R. Lawrence, Jung-eun Lim, Jiaqi Huang, Joshua N. Sampson, Stephanie J. Weinstein, Demetrius A...
abstract: Serum metabolites were analyzed in relation to alpha-tocopherol levels in men from the ATBC Study. Many lipid and amino acid metabolites were associated with alpha-tocopherol, suggesting potential mechanisms for vitamin E's health effects.

title: Preventive effects of nitrate-rich beetroot juice supplementation on monocrotaline-induced pulmonary hypertension in rats
authors: Masashi Tawa, Rikako Nagata, Yuiko Sumi, Keisuke Nakagawa, Tatsuya Sawano, Mamoru Ohkita, Yasuo Mats...
abstract: Beetroot juice supplementation was studied for its preventive effects on a rat model of pulmonary hypertension. A low dose of beetroot juice, but not a high dose, prevented pulmonary hypertension, suggesting a nitrate-dependent mechanism.

title: Training for a (half‐)marathon: Training volume and longest endurance run related to performance and running injuries
authors: Tryntsje Fokkema, Ankie A.D.N. van Damme, Maarten W.J. Fornerod, Robert‐Jan de Vos, Sita M.A. Bierma...
abstract: Training volume and longest endurance runs were studied in relation to marathon performance and injuries. Higher training volumes and longer endurance runs were associated with faster finish times, without an increased risk of injury.

title: Lessening Organ Dysfunction With Vitamin C (LOVIT) Trial: Statistical Analysis Plan
authors: Neill KJ Adhikari, Ruxandra Pinto, Andrew G Day, Marie-Hélène Masse, Julie Ménard, Sheila Sprague, D...
abstract: This paper details the statistical analysis plan for the LOVIT trial, which investigates intravenous vitamin C for critically ill patients with infection. The plan outlines analyses for a composite primary outcome of mortality and persistent organ dysfunction at 28 days.

title: Comparison of α-Tocopherol, α-Tocopherol Acetate, and α-Tocopheryl Polyethylene Glycol Succinate 1000 Absorption by Caco-2 TC7 Intestinal Cells
authors: Charlotte Cuerq, Claire Bordat, Charlotte Halimi, Emilie Blond, Marion Nowicki, Noël Peretti, Emmanu...
abstract: This study compared the absorption of vitamin E forms by Caco-2 cells. TPGS showed the lowest secretion, with esterified forms of vitamin E being secreted basolaterally.

title: Influence of pre and postpartum alpha-tocopherol supplementation on milk yield, milk quality, and udder health of Jersey crossbred cows at tropical lower Gangetic region
authors: Amit Kumar Singh, Champak Bhakat, Tripti Kumari, Dilip Kumar Mandal, Anupam Chatterjee, Muthupalani ...
abstract: This study investigated alpha-tocopherol supplementation's effects on Jersey crossbred cows. Supplementation improved milk yield, quality, and udder health, especially with longer postpartum administration.

title: Effect of Dietary Nitrate and Anthocyanins on Anaerobic Exercise in Untrained Individuals
Colostrum supplementation with n-3 fatty acids and α-tocopherol alters plasma polyunsaturated fatty acid profile and decreases an indicator of oxidative stress in newborn calves
authors: Julie Opgenorth, Lorraine M. Sordillo, Michael J. VandeHaar
abstract: Newborn calves were supplemented with n-3 fatty acids and α-tocopherol in colostrum. This supplementation reduced an indicator of oxidative stress in the first week of life.

title: Effect of Ethanol on Parthenogenetic Activation and α-Tocopherol Supplementation during  In Vitro  Maturation on Developmental Competence of Summer-Collected Bovine Oocytes
authors: Francisco Báez, Belén Gómez, Victoria de Brun, Nélida Rodríguez-Osorio, Carolina Viñoles
abstract: This study investigated ethanol's effect on parthenogenetic activation and α-tocopherol's impact on bovine oocyte competence during in vitro maturation. 100 μM α-tocopherol, diluted in 0.05% ethanol, improved embryonic quality by reducing apoptosis and increasing SOD2 expression.

title: Choline and methionine supplementation in layer hens fed flaxseed: effects on hen production performance, egg fatty acid composition, tocopherol content, and oxidative stability
authors: M.H. Beheshti Moghadam, A.E. Aziza, G. Cherian
abstract: This study investigated choline and methionine supplementation in layer hens fed flaxseed. Supplementation improved production performance, increased n-3 fatty acids and tocopherol, and reduced lipid oxidation.

title: Effect of retinol and α-tocopherol supplementation on photoreceptor and retinal ganglion cell apoptosis in diabetic rats model
authors: Andi Muhammad Ichsan, Agussalim Bukhari, Subehan Lallo, Upik Anderiani Miskad, Andi Afdal Dzuhry, It...
source: International Journal of Retina and Vitreous
abstract: Retinol and α-tocopherol were supplemented to diabetic rats to study their effects on retinal cells. α-tocopherol showed the most promise in preventing photoreceptor and retinal ganglion cell apoptosis.

title: The effect of finishing diet supplemented with methionine/lysine and methionine/ α -tocopherol on performance, carcass traits and meat quality of Hanwoo steers
authors: Farouq Heidar Barido, Dicky Tri Utama, Hae Song Jong, Juntae Kim, Chang Woo Lee, Yeon Soo Park, Sung...
abstract: Diets supplemented with methionine/lysine or methionine/α-tocopherol were fed to Hanwoo steers. Methionine/lysine improved meat tenderness and water holding capacity, while methionine/α-tocopherol enhanced meat color, reduced oxidation, and increased tenderness.

title: Can Bioactive Compounds in Beetroot/Carrot Juice Have a Neuroprotective Effect? Morphological Studies of Neurons Immunoreactive to Calretinin of the Rat Hippocampus after Exposure to Cadmium
authors: Małgorzata Matysek, Edyta Kowalczuk-Vasilev, Radosław Szalak, Ewa Baranowska-Wójcik, Marcin B. Arcis...
abstract: Cadmium exposure reduced calretinin-expressing neurons and nerve fibers in rat hippocampus. Beetroot/carrot juice attenuated these negative effects, suggesting neuroprotective potential.

title: Soybean Callus—A Potential Source of Tocopherols
authors: Liliana Mureșan, Doina Clapa, Teodor Rusu, Thomas T. Y. Wang, Jae B. Park
abstract: Soybean callus was studied for tocopherol content and compared to conventionally grown soybeans. Soybean callus contains significantly higher levels of tocopherols than soybean seeds, and herbicides influence callus production and tocopherol content.

title: Effect of Processing and Storage on the Quality of Beetroot and Apple Mixed Juice
authors: Flavia Bianchi, Marina Pünsch, Elena Venir
abstract: Beetroot and apple juice blends were studied for quality changes during processing and storage. Apple juice addition reduced antioxidant activity, while pasteurization and storage decreased betalains and color.

title: Degradation of Patulin in Pear Juice and Apple Juice by Ascorbic Acid and the Combination of Ascorbic Acid and Ferrous Iron
authors: Xiaoyan Wei, Mengyao Du, Sung-Yong Hong, Ae-Son Om
abstract: Ascorbic acid and its combination with ferrous iron were tested for patulin degradation in pear and apple juices. Ascorbic acid alone degraded patulin effectively, with the combination showing even higher degradation rates.

title: Vitamin C: a misunderstood ally?
authors: Jiajia Ren, Xuting Jin, Ya Gao, Ruohan Li, Jiamei Li, Jingjing Zhang, Xiaochuang Wang, Gang Wang

title: Resistance Exercise and Cardiovascular Disease in Diabetes Mellitus
authors: Jin-Hwan Yoon

title: Vitamin C in human health and disease
authors: Seyed Ali Khonsary

title: Vitamin C, respiratory infections and the immune system
authors: Harri Hemilä

title: Determination of selenium species in beetroot juices
authors: Aleksandra Sentkowska, Krystyna Pyrzynska
abstract: Beetroot juices were analyzed for selenium species and antioxidant properties. Organic beetroot juice contained the highest selenomethionine and exhibited the strongest radical scavenging ability.
